findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
findings.body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, line 70 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `VIEW` is included in the expected scopes, any admin granted only the `view` scope on the `Groups` (all-groups) resource will have `canManage()` return `true`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards group creation and moving groups to the top level with `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin with only `view` permission on all groups can create top-level groups or move existing groups to top level. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource ID instead of group ID (resource name) and ignores resource type on creation
findings.body:
In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` is used to find group resources, and then `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` are called. There are three issues here:
1. When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a per-group resource (lines 121-127 of `AdminPermissionsSchema.java`), it sets the resource's `name` to `group.getId()`, while `resource.getId()` is a newly generated resource UUID, and it never calls `resource.setType(...)` on individual resources (only the 'all-groups' resource created in `init()` has `type = "Groups"`). As a result, `findByType` will not find individual group resources at all.
2. `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Passing `groupResource.getId()` (the resource UUID) instead of `groupResource.getName()` (the group UUID) causes `findByName` to return `null` and fall back to the all-groups resource.
3. `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authorization `Resource` UUID instead of the `GroupModel` ID (`groupResource.getName()`), so subsequent user queries filtering by `UserModel.GROUPS` will not match any group memberships.

findings.title: User search restricts results to group members even when admin has permission to view users directly
findings.body: In `UsersResource.searchForUser` (and identically in `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` at line 147), the `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard was removed before calling `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. Additionally, in FGAP V2, an admin can have `view` permission on specific individual users (without global `auth.users().canView()`) AND `view-members` permission on a group. When `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` is set, the user storage query restricts the DB search to *only* members of `groupIds`, which filters out any users outside those groups that the admin had direct user-level permission to view, and also sets `usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(true)` (line 459), which in `UserPermissions` bypasses per-user view checks.

findings.title: AdminPermissionsSchema does not handle Group resources in getResourceName and resolveGroup
findings.body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 328-350), only `USERS.getType()` is handled to resolve a human-readable name (`"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`). For `GROUPS` (and `CLIENTS`), `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource`, causing policy/permission representations returned by the API to have `null` resource names instead of the group name or `"All groups"`.
